title: Sliceable commitments and proportional backpressure router for deferred capacity smoothing
author: Priya Kumar
release_notes: Introduces sliceable capacity commitments and a proportional backpressure router to smooth deferred capacity spikes and improve tail latency under bursty workloads.
description: Context: Customers observed that short, high-intensity microbursts cause non-linear cost spikes and transient SLA violations even when long-term reservations exist. Motivation: Provide a mechanism to both preserve long-term commitment economics and absorb short bursts without immediate large-scale provisioning. This PR introduces two complementary subsystems: 1) Sliceable Commitments - reservations can be partitioned into time-slices and weight-slices so that short-lived microbursts consume 'slices' before triggering full provisioning. Sliceable commitments expose a lightweight API for the allocator to reserve and reclaim fractional capacity bounded by tenant SLAs. 2) Proportional Backpressure Router - a routing layer that applies graded backpressure across capacity tiers proportional to real-time reservation slice consumption and headroom signals. The router integrates TTL-decayed utilization fingerprints and region affinity to prefer warm pools but gracefully degrade to burst-capable pools when required. Design summary: The changes include a new commitments API, a slice accounting engine, an admission controller that consults slice budgets and latency-tail budgets, and a router component that computes per-request pressure scores to decide routing/fallback. New telemetry hooks emit slice consumption, slice-reclaim events, soft-fallback counts, and per-tenant tail-latency deltas. Rollout plan: gated feature flag per-cluster, opt-in via tenant profile, and staged canary with internal infra and two pilot customers. Backwards compatibility: default behavior unchanged if sliceable reservations are not enabled. Tests: unit tests for slice accounting, integration test harness that replays historical burst traces showing 35–45% reduction in cold-provision ramp-ups, and load tests verifying tail-p99 latency improvement under synthetic microbursts. Checklist: - [x] API and proto changes documented - [x] Migration path for existing reservations - [x] Telemetry dashboards and alert rules added - [x] E2E canary run plan attached - [x] Performance benchmarks included

review_comments: Ethan McCoy: Nice direction. A few implementation notes: 1) please ensure the slice reclaim path is idempotent and defensively coded against races, 2) add a dashboard for stale slices so ops can detect reclaim leaks.

Lina Ortega: Can we quantify cost impact at 10% sustained burst saturation? Also please add more comments around the pressure scoring formula — it's dense.

Priya Kumar: Added a short explainer in proportional_router.go and appended a summary in docs/migrations; ran cost sims — at 10% sustained microburst saturation we expect ~12% lower peak provisioning costs vs current baseline.
